report:
Wrote the cleaned backlog to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-liammagnier-Developer-project-juno/bfdee244-0283-4629-a3f4-3c603fc89908/scratchpad/merge/backlog.clean.json. It has the same shape as the input: {items[101], anti_patterns[76]}, the same keys and order, the same indent=1 and UTF-8 formatting, and it is valid JSON. No item or anti-pattern was dropped. Every changed item still stands on Juno's own audit (its juno_today and defect ids are untouched) plus non-leak sources. The script that made the edits is /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-liammagnier-Developer-project-juno/bfdee244-0283-4629-a3f4-3c603fc89908/scratchpad/merge/clean_backlog.py. It makes 37 exact-match replacements, each checked to occur exactly once, and asserts that no leak markers remain.

What I checked:
- Every text field of all 101 items and 76 anti-patterns (reference, recommendation, juno_today, user_value, title, pattern, why).
- Explicit leak mentions, and leak-only facts that appear without the word "leak". I searched for these facts by their own terms: streaming paint, placeholders, the tweaks panel's geometry and material, deck-stage, animated-video, ask_user, the Options recipe, !important overrides, the verifier, random style choices, "SOMETHING should always be in motion", the handoff README contents, napkin/scraps, and data-comment-anchor.
- Leak links: none were present in the backlog.
- Every "community"-tagged reference. The others (HN, forums, App Store, Caipi, Rui Quintino, adrianroselli) are not leaks and were kept.
- Quoted passages: none is longer than 25 words (the longest is 18).
- The remaining words "leak", "leaks" and "leaked" describe Juno's own defects (M31, M46, R-015 backfill, and "Revoking a leaked link") and were kept.

Leak-only material removed or re-justified:
- **R-033:** removed the leaked prompt line about painting from the first streamed character. The streaming recommendation still rests on the first-hand Claude Docs skeleton contract, the visualize contract, Google Stitch, the Builder.io/UX Pilot timing, and Juno's X-07/M14/M15.
- **R-043:**
  - Replaced the leak bullet (bottom-right, 280px) with first-hand evidence: tweaks are typed data-props shown as levers (claude-primary-evidence.md).
  - The recommendation's tweak taxonomy ("behaviour, alternative treatments, cross-cutting flags; never copy or single colours") came from the leak. It now reads: spacing, colour and layout, the levers Anthropic's launch post names, and not copy.
  - The 280px width is now justified by Juno's own inspector width (R-017).
  - "not Claude's panel material values" was dropped.
- **R-045:**
  - Removed the leaked ask_user bullet (13 kinds, 6-10 questions, decide-for-me). It is rewritten from PCWorld and Builder.io: Claude Design asks multiple-choice questions, about a minute, a "taste exam" that uses the whole canvas.
  - The resolution no longer mentions random numbers.
- **R-046:** removed the leaked Options-recipe bullet. In the recommendation, "'Try next' chips" became "follow-up suggestion chips". The item still rests on Lenny's, Builder.io, Stitch and Juno's single-proposal gap.
- **R-057:** removed the leaked deck-stage bullet.
- **R-083:** removed the leaked animated-video skill bullet.
- **Anti-pattern 23:** "!important override blocks (Claude Design leak)" became "HTML artboards whose properties panel rewrites inline styles (Claude's Design type)". That wording is supported first-hand.
- **Anti-pattern 24:** dropped the attribution of a per-turn screenshot verifier to standalone Claude Design.
- **Anti-pattern 26:** removed the random-numbers claim. The Figma Make Designs example remains.
- **Anti-pattern 47:** removed "forms close when the user types in chat". It keeps Builder.io's auto-send finding.
- **Anti-pattern 56:** removed the "SOMETHING should always be in motion" quote and the "Claude leak" attribution. It keeps HN (rotating tips), the ChatGPT Apps SDK and the Figma mockups.

Desktop-app values (rule 4):
- Every "(bundle…)" citation now reads "observed in the shipped Claude desktop app", with the primary tag kept where it was there. This covers R-007, 008, 013, 014, 016, 021, 023, 024, 034, 063, 068, 070, 071, 072, 077 and 095.
- Anti-patterns 19 and 57 gained the same attribution because they carry values.
- Two internal identifiers were replaced with plain words: R-008 "sheet-kind system" and anti-pattern 61 "CDS ladder".
- Short user-visible strings under 25 words were kept, for example the conflict copy, "Artifact panel: {title}" and the Motion setting label.

Judgement calls for the orchestrator:
- Some Juno recommendations that echo leaked ideas were kept as Juno's own design decisions, justified by their stated reasons and not attributed to Claude:
  - R-045: the Decide-for-me button, 2-4 wireframe options, and typing adding an answer.
  - R-046: the 1a/1b badge ids and new rounds stacking above.
  - R-057: frames staying mounted, ?frame=, and the idle fade of the player bar.
  - R-066: the handoff README with interactions and easing (Juno already ships a handoff bundle, per 01-AUDIT-WEB).
- If a stricter reading is wanted, these are the places to trim.
- Builder.io's auto-send finding comes from the claude-design research lens, not from 03-COMPETITIVE-AUDIT.md.

Not in scope and still containing leak text:
- The sibling files competitive/backlog.md and the generator sources competitive/bl_*.py. If backlog.md is used downstream, it should be rebuilt from the cleaned JSON.
- /Users/liammagnier/Developer/project/juno/docs/design/artifacts-design/03-COMPETITIVE-AUDIT.md, when last read, still had the leak links (lines 91, 316, 337, 385, 407, 1615) and the leak in its [C] tag definition (line 19). Presumably another pass is cleaning it.

I edited no product code, doc files or repo files.
